Neil Fox Way: Residents and drivers urged to plan ahead due to road closures for Wakefield Hospice 5K Night Run

By Leanne Clarke
Published 29th Sep 2026, 09:00 BST

People are being urged to plan ahead as the popular Wakefield Hospice 5K Night Run returns this Saturday (October 3) after a seven-year absence.

Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 1:40
Instaread

The much-loved event will bring runners to the streets of Wakefield, with temporary road closures put in place to keep participants, spectators and residents safe.

Neil Fox Way will be closed from the Novale Way roundabout to the roundabout near the River Calder between 6.15pm and 8.30pm.

A number of adjoining roads will also be affected.

Signed diversion routes will be in operation, with motorists asked to follow the temporary signage and allow extra time for their journeys.

Residents whose properties can only be accessed via Neil Fox Way are being advised that vehicle access in or out of the affected area will not be possible during the closure.

Anyone who may need their vehicle during the evening is encouraged to move it before 6.15pm. Vehicles can also be parked at Wakefield Hospice ahead of the closure if required.

Alexander Cunniff, Community and Events Manager at Wakefield Hospice, said the closures were essential to ensure the event could take place safely.

“We would like to offer our sincerest gratitude not just to all those taking part, but to the entire Wakefield community for their understanding regarding the road closures associated with this event.”

He added: “We understand these temporary restrictions may cause inconvenience, particularly for residents and businesses directly affected by the closure.

“We sincerely apologise for any disruption this may cause and greatly appreciate your patience, understanding and support.”

Places are still available for the Night Run. Anyone wanting to take part can find out more and sign up here.
